title: Anvil-based hook integration test: block-pinned regression + current-head smoke test
goal: Test the hook's swap path against real deployed Uniswap v4 bytecode with two distinct fork suites — a block-pinned reproducible suite for review/regression and a separate current-head smoke test for drift detection — per security-and-evidence.md, not one implicitly-current-head run.
steps: Extend RobinhoodV4PoolManager.t.sol's pattern (already deploys a real PoolManager/PositionManager from the pinned Uniswap submodules) into two suites

RobinhoodV4Fork.t.sol: fork at a fixed, recorded block number (pinned in the test file, not read from the environment at runtime) so the suite is byte-for-byte reproducible and reviewable; this is the suite CI runs on every change and a reviewer actually reads

RobinhoodV4ForkSmoke.t.sol: fork at current head (no pinned block), run only a minimal smoke path, and treat its failure as 'the pinned block's assumptions have drifted from live chain state, go re-pin and investigate' rather than 'the hook is broken' — mark it non-blocking/scheduled in CI, not a required check
Run the full swap path (with and without hookData) against the forked, real deployed bytecode in both suites
Assert the WP-02 fee-conformance and WP-05 optional-hookData behavior both hold against the pinned-block fork, not just the hand-written test harness
acceptance: The hook's swap path passes against real deployed PoolManager/PositionManager bytecode on a fork pinned to a fixed, recorded block number
A separate current-head smoke suite exists and is distinguishable in CI output from the pinned-block regression suite
Both the hookData-present and hookData-optional paths are exercised against the pinned-block fork
notes: Read-only fork tests, no key needed; the pinned-block suite is safe to run in CI on every change, the current-head smoke suite runs on a schedule and is non-blocking.
